Name: breadth_routed_memory
Title: Consolidate the Broad, Retrieve the Narrow: Coverage — Not Utility, Not Usage — Decides Where Agent Experience Should Live
Short Hypothesis: Whether a distilled agent-experience item should be written into the always-on instruction or left in a retrieval-gated bank is determined by its *coverage breadth* — the fraction of the deployment query distribution for which it enters the top-k — and not by its utility (how much it helps when it fires) nor by its historical usage frequency (how often it was retrieved in past traffic). Broad items occupy scarce top-k slots on nearly every episode and crowd out narrow items that would have helped the few queries they match; consolidating broad items into the instruction frees those slots. The prediction that separates this from classical caching is inverted: a hit-rate-maximizing cache promotes broad items *into* the fast tier to serve them faster, whereas we claim the value of promotion is that it *removes* the broad item from the competitive tier. Therefore a breadth-routed hybrid beats both pure always-on playbooks and pure top-k retrieval at a matched token budget, the gain arrives through narrow items newly entering the top-k rather than through the consolidated text, breadth beats usage-frequency routing exactly when past traffic is skewed relative to deployment traffic, and the effect shrinks when the retrieval mechanism does not enforce a fixed slot count.
Related Work:
Three literatures converge on this decision and none of them has run the experiment.

**(i) Always-on evolving context.** Dynamic Cheatsheet (Suzgun et al., 2025) and agentic-context-engineering / playbook methods maintain one growing block of distilled experience present in every prompt. They never ask which items deserve permanent residency.

**(ii) Retrieval-gated episodic memory.** ExpeL (AAAI 2024), Agent Workflow Memory (ICML 2025), Synapse, and ReasoningBank-style 2025/26 systems key a bank on the query and inject a fixed top-k. They never ask which items should be promoted out of the bank. On the optimizer side, MIPROv2 (EMNLP 2024) jointly optimizes an instruction and a *fixed* bootstrapped demonstration set — chosen once, not retrieval-gated, with no per-item notion of coverage — and GEPA evolves instruction text with the memory slot untouched. Reviewers were right that MIPROv2 is the most direct existing instantiation of "couple the instruction with a demonstration set," so it is now a first-class arm (E2 vii) rather than an omission.

**(iii) Memory tiering and classical caching.** MemGPT's core/archival paging and A-MEM's consolidation promote frequently-accessed or recent items into an always-resident tier. Behind them sits four decades of cache admission/eviction theory: Belady's optimal replacement (route by *future* access), LFU/LRU/ARC (route by *past* access), and working-set estimation (estimate future access from a representative recent window). A reviewer correctly observed that "estimate future access from deployment-representative data rather than stale logs" is, at the level of slogan, working-set estimation. We concede that and state precisely what does not carry over:
- **The tiers are not equivalent.** In a cache, the fast and slow tier return the same object with different latency; a miss costs time. Here, instruction residency changes the *content and framing* of the prompt (merged, always present, no gating) and a miss costs a wrong answer, not a delay.
- **The competitive tier is always full.** Top-k always injects exactly k items, so admitting one item evicts another on *every* query. Caches have idle capacity and variable occupancy; this is a permanent zero-sum allocation.
- **The optimal move is inverted.** A hit-rate-maximizing cache promotes the broadest item into the fast tier *to serve it*. We claim promotion is valuable because it *vacates a slot in the competitive tier* — a benefit with no analogue in caching, where fast-tier residency does not free slow-tier capacity. This is exactly what the refill / no-refill / padding controls test, and no capacity-driven paging paper runs them.
- **The objective is accuracy, not hit rate,** which makes it non-obvious that coverage should dominate value. The surprising part of our claim is that a *label-free* coverage statistic beats a *label-expensive* utility statistic.

The pilot behind this track showed the harmful bank retrieved *topically correct* items and that injection **volume** was the causal lever — which is what slot competition predicts and relevance-based accounts of memory harm do not.
Abstract: Agent frameworks store distilled experience in one of two places: an always-on block shipped with every prompt (playbook / cheatsheet methods) or a retrieval-gated bank from which a fixed top-k is injected per query (ExpeL-style memory). The two have never been compared at a matched token budget, and the intermediate question — which items should be promoted into the instruction and which should stay retrievable — has been answered in practice only by usage-frequency paging (MemGPT) and, in theory, by classical cache admission policies. We propose an economic account with a prediction that inverts the caching one. Instruction residency costs tokens on every episode but guarantees availability; bank residency costs tokens only when retrieved but competes for a scarce, always-full set of injection slots. This makes **coverage breadth** — the fraction of the *deployment* query distribution for which an item enters top-k — the deciding statistic, because a broad item occupies a slot on nearly every episode and starves narrow items. Unlike a cache, which promotes broad items to serve them faster, we predict the benefit of promotion is the *vacated slot*. Breadth is computable from unlabeled calibration queries; utility requires labeled probes; usage frequency is measured on past traffic and misleads whenever past traffic is skewed. We test this on multi-hop QA with a local search index and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: an item-level placement regression with breadth, utility and usage entered as competing predictors; a matched-token comparison of no-memory, pure top-k, similarity-threshold retrieval, pure playbook, MemGPT-style usage promotion, MIPROv2 joint instruction+demonstrations, and breadth routing; slot-freeing controls (refill / no-refill / padding) at k=2 where slots are scarcest; oracle-breadth and oracle-placement ceilings that bound the headroom the free statistic leaves on the table; a second dataset (MuSiQue) for the primary contrast; and a threshold-retrieval replication that tests whether the mechanism is specific to fixed-k. Everything is item-paired with McNemar contrasts against a measured null-replicate floor. Total program: 28,300 episodes, ~35 wall-clock hours on one 4×A100 node and under $100 of API.
Experiments:
**Setup.** Task: multi-hop QA. Primary dataset HotpotQA full-wiki; second dataset MuSiQue-Ans (fallback 2WikiMultihopQA if the 7B ReAct agent's base EM on MuSiQue is <15%). Retrieval tool is a **local BM25+dense Wikipedia index** — free, deterministic, cacheable, no API cost and no tool-side noise. Scoring is **exact match** (secondary F1); **no LLM judge**. Agent: ReAct, ~4 LLM calls/episode. Model: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, greedy, fixed seeds. Memory bank: ExpeL/ReasoningBank-style, ~300 items (distilled insights plus successful/failed trajectory summaries) built by a frontier model from 500 history episodes; dense retrieval (bge-large), top-k injection.

**Splits (all disjoint).** *History stream*: 500 episodes with a deliberate **Zipfian topic skew**, used for bank construction and usage counts. *Calibration set*: 500 **unlabeled** queries from the deployment distribution, used only to compute breadth and cutoffs. *Validation*: 300 labeled, for k, similarity cutoff, breadth cutoff. *Held-out*: 800 labeled, paired across all conditions.

**The three routing statistics, separated by construction.**
- **Breadth** b(m) = fraction of the 500 unlabeled calibration queries for which m enters top-k. Zero labels, zero LLM calls.
- **Usage frequency** f(m) = recency-weighted retrieval count over the skewed history stream (the MemGPT/A-MEM/LFU signal). The skew is what makes f and b diverge: a narrow item serving a common past topic gets high f, low b; a general-strategy item distilled from a rare topic gets low f, high b.
- **Utility** u(m) = paired outcome change from single-item injection, estimated with 6 probes each on the 60 highest-retrieval-mass items (360 episodes).

**E0 (Gate and decorrelation check).** (a) Does the bank matter at all: top-k vs no-memory on held-out, in either direction, beyond the measured noise floor. (b) Report Spearman ρ(b,f), ρ(b,u), and the Lorenz curve of retrieval mass. Pre-registered rule: if ρ(b,f) > 0.7, the breadth-vs-frequency arm is declared uninformative *in this setup* and reported as such — no post hoc manufacture of separation; same rule for ρ(b,u). If (a) fails, the paper becomes the matched-token comparison plus a bounded null, stated up front. Cost: validation sweeps for k / similarity cutoff / breadth cutoff (300 × ~7 configs = 2,100) + 360 utility probes + 40 slack = **2,500**.

**E1 (Item-level placement law — the core test).** 14 items spanning the breadth range. For each: (a) item in the instruction, removed from the bank; (b) item in the bank only. Each scored on the same 150 held-out queries, **stratified 75 where m ∈ top-k and 75 where m ∉ top-k**, shared seeds. Four items also get (c) absent entirely. Placement advantage A(m) = acc(instr) − acc(bank), regressed on b(m) in a mixed-effects logistic model with item and query random intercepts and fixed effects for b, u, f and item length. **The tested quantity is the breadth coefficient**, not any single item. A(m) for these 14 items is also the ground truth for the oracle ceiling in E6. Episodes: 14×2×150 + 4×150 = **4,800**.

**E2 (Matched-token system comparison, n=800 paired, k* tuned on validation).** Seven arms, matched on logged mean realized prompt tokens within 5%: (i) no memory; (ii) pure top-k retrieval; (iii) **similarity-threshold retrieval** (variable count above a calibrated cutoff) — the arm that could dissolve the slot-scarcity premise; (iv) pure playbook (highest-utility items merged into an always-on block to budget, no retrieval); (v) **usage-frequency promotion, MemGPT-style** (promote by recency-weighted f, evict on capacity, remainder retrievable); (vi) **breadth-routed hybrid** (consolidate items above the validation-calibrated breadth cutoff into a merged block, remainder retrievable at fixed k, freed slots refilled); (vii) **MIPROv2-style joint optimization** — instruction plus a fixed bootstrapped demonstration set, no retrieval gating, optimization capped at 400 rollouts. Arm (vii) replaces the GEPA-no-memory arm from the previous version, per review: it is the closest existing instantiation of instruction+demonstration coupling and the honest test of whether fixed jointly-optimized demos already buy what breadth routing buys. Episodes: 7×800 + 400 optimization = **6,000**.

**E3 (Slot-freeing controls, at k=2 where slots are scarcest and the predicted effect largest).** (a) breadth hybrid with refill, n=800; (b) same, no refill (freed slots left empty, effective k drops), n=800; (c) drop-only (broad items deleted, no consolidation, refill), n=600; (d) padding (broad items consolidated, freed slots filled with length-matched neutral text), n=600; (e) pure retrieval k=2, n=600. Running at k=2 rather than k=4 is a pre-registered power decision. Episodes: **3,400**.

**E4 (Routing-variable ablation, matched consolidated-token budget, all with refill).** Utility-routed (n=800) and random-routed (n=800) versus breadth (reuse E2 vi) and skewed-frequency (reuse E2 v). Plus **frequency routing computed on an unskewed history stream** (n=400), predicted to converge on breadth routing — the positive control showing the breadth/frequency distinction is about distribution shift, not naming. Episodes: **2,000**.

**E5 (Attribution, free from logs).** For every held-out item the breadth hybrid fixes relative to pure retrieval, record whether its top-k retrieved set changed.

**E6 (Headroom / oracle ceilings) — added per review.** (a) **Oracle-breadth**: breadth recomputed on the 800 held-out queries themselves rather than the calibration sample; the gap to E2 (vi) is pure calibration sampling error. (b) **Oracle-placement**: for the 14 E1 items, place each on the side that E1's held-out-measured A(m) says is better, all other items routed by breadth; the gap to E2 (vi) restricted to those items bounds how much of the achievable placement gain the free statistic captures. n=800 each. Episodes: **1,600**.

**E7 (Second-dataset replication of the primary contrast) — added per review.** MuSiQue-Ans: fresh bank (300 episodes of construction, same skewed-history protocol), 200 unlabeled calibration queries, then four arms at n=600 paired — pure top-k, pure playbook, usage-frequency promotion, breadth hybrid. This tests P2 and the frequency half of P4 on a genuinely different compositional-question distribution. It is a *dataset-level* replication, not a task-family generalization, and is labeled as such. Episodes: 300 + 200 + 4×600 = **2,900**.

**E8 (Retrieval-architecture replication) — added per review.** Breadth hybrid layered on **similarity-threshold retrieval** instead of fixed-k, n=600, compared to the threshold baseline from E2 (iii). Prediction: the hybrid's margin is *smaller* here than under fixed-k, because variable-count admission does not force broad items to evict narrow ones. This converts the reviewer's "the mechanism may be a fixed-k artifact" objection into a signed prediction. Episodes: **600**.

**Noise and variance budget.** Null replicate: rerun pure retrieval k* in full with fresh seeds and score it against itself (800). Three decoding seeds on two key cells at n=400 (1,600). Playbook merge is stochastic: two extra merges for the hybrid and for pure playbook at n=400 (1,600). Total **4,000**.

**Compute arithmetic.** 500 (HotpotQA bank) + 2,500 (E0) + 4,800 (E1) + 6,000 (E2) + 3,400 (E3) + 2,000 (E4) + 1,600 (E6) + 2,900 (E7) + 600 (E8) + 4,000 (noise) = **28,300 episodes**. At ~4 LLM calls/episode ≈ 113k calls, ~1.5k prompt and ~250 output tokens each ⇒ ~170M prefill, ~28M decode. On the 4×A100 node running four vLLM replicas of a 7B model at high concurrency against a free local index, pilot throughput ~800 episodes/hour end-to-end gives **~35 wall-clock hours (~140 GPU-hours)**; we budget 4 days for reruns and orchestration. Frontier-API use is confined to bank distillation (~800 calls across two datasets), playbook merges (~40) and MIPROv2 instruction proposal (~50) — **under $100**.

**Cut and not deferred:** ALFWorld/WebShop, the 3-model grid, the bank-size sweep, the homogeneous-bank replication, the k=8 probe, the GEPA-no-memory arm, and the 14B secondary check. Each was removed because it did not decide a claim, and the freed episodes were spent on the three reviewer-named additions (MIPROv2 arm, oracle ceilings, second dataset) plus the threshold-architecture replication.
Baselines and Ablations:
Baselines that could plausibly win, all at matched realized token budget on the same paired held-out items:
1. **Pure top-k retrieval**, k tuned on validation — the standard agent-memory configuration.
2. **Similarity-threshold (variable-count) retrieval** — if it matches the hybrid at matched tokens, the fixed-k slot-scarcity framing is mechanism-specific, and we report that as the paper's corrected conclusion. E8 makes this a graded rather than binary test.
3. **Usage-frequency promotion, MemGPT/A-MEM/LFU style** — the closest deployed policy. If it matches breadth routing under skewed history, the contribution reduces to a measured explanation of why an existing heuristic works, plus the slot-competition mechanism.
4. **Pure playbook** (Dynamic-Cheatsheet / ACE style always-on block) at the same budget.
5. **MIPROv2-style joint instruction + fixed bootstrapped demonstrations** (added per review) — tests whether jointly-optimized static demos already capture what breadth routing buys.
6. **Drop-only** — the cheapest possible fix. If deleting broad items matches consolidating them, the consolidation machinery is unnecessary.
7. **No memory** and **k=2 unscreened retrieval** (the volume-reduction neutralizer from the pilot).
8. **Oracle-breadth** and **oracle-placement** ceilings (added per review) — bound the headroom left by the free statistic, so a 3-point win over MemGPT can be read as near-optimal or as leaving most of the gain unclaimed.

Ablations isolating the mechanism: (a) refill vs no-refill vs padding-filled freed slots at k=2 — separates slot-freeing from token savings and from duplicate removal; (b) breadth vs utility vs usage-frequency vs random routing at matched consolidated tokens; (c) frequency routing on an unskewed history stream, predicted to converge on breadth — the control proving breadth and frequency are different variables rather than two names for one; (d) LLM-merged playbook vs verbatim concatenation of the same items; (e) instruction length matched by appending neutral text to pure retrieval; (f) cost accounting for the routing statistic itself — breadth needs 0 labeled episodes, utility needed 360.
Falsifiable Predictions:
Minimum detectable effect: n=800 paired at ~12% discordance ⇒ ≈2.5 EM points; n=600 ⇒ ≈2.9. Thresholds are set above these and anything smaller is pre-committed to "indistinguishable," not "trend."

**P1 (placement law).** In E1 the breadth coefficient in the mixed-effects placement regression is positive with a 95% CI excluding zero, after conditioning on utility, usage frequency and item length. Refutation: flat or negative slope — placement does not depend on breadth, which kills the theory.

**P2 (routing beats both endpoints).** At matched tokens the breadth-routed hybrid beats pure top-k retrieval by ≥3 EM points and pure playbook by ≥3 points on HotpotQA (n=800), and beats pure top-k by ≥3.5 points on MuSiQue (n=600). Refutation: within 2.5 points of the better endpoint on the primary dataset — the honest result is then "placement does not matter once tokens are matched," and the matched-token comparison (including the threshold, MemGPT and MIPROv2 arms nobody has run head-to-head) is the contribution.

**P3 (slot-freeing is the mechanism).** At k=2, hybrid-with-refill beats hybrid-without-refill by ≥3 points and beats the padding control by ≥3.5 points (n=600 for padding). Powered only if the total hybrid gain at k=2 is ≥4 points; if smaller we declare the mechanism contrast underpowered rather than reporting a null as evidence. Refutation: no-refill matches refill — the benefit is token savings or duplicate removal, not slot competition.

**P4 (coverage, not utility, not usage).** Breadth routing beats utility routing by ≥3 points at equal consolidated tokens; beats MemGPT-style usage-frequency routing by ≥3 points on HotpotQA and ≥3.5 on MuSiQue under skewed history; and frequency routing on the **unskewed** stream lands within 2.5 points of breadth routing (positive control). Utility and frequency are not significant predictors of placement advantage after conditioning on breadth (E1). Refutation: utility or usage matches breadth under skew, or the unskewed control fails to converge.

**P5 (attribution).** ≥70% of the hybrid's fixes relative to pure retrieval occur on held-out items whose top-k retrieved set changed. Refutation: fixes spread uniformly, implying the consolidated text itself does the work.

**P6 (headroom).** Oracle-breadth is within 2.5 points of calibration-breadth (the free statistic is not sampling-limited), and calibration-breadth recovers ≥50% of the oracle-placement gain restricted to the 14 E1 items. A large oracle-placement gap does not refute the theory but bounds the practical claim, and we report it as such.

**P7 (mechanism is slot-count-dependent, not universal).** The hybrid's margin over its own retrieval baseline is larger under fixed-k (E2) than under similarity-threshold retrieval (E8), by ≥3 points in the difference-of-differences at the pooled n. If threshold retrieval fully matches the fixed-k hybrid at matched tokens, the general "economic law of placement" framing is refuted and the corrected headline is that slot competition is an artifact of fixed-k admission — which is itself a finding worth reporting, since fixed-k is what every deployed agent-memory system uses.
Measurement and Noise Control:
All conditions are scored on identical held-out items with identical decoding seeds; the unit of analysis is the per-item outcome change. Pairwise contrasts use McNemar's exact test on discordant pairs, with **fixes and breaks reported separately**, because the pilot showed net deltas can be flat while composition shifts. Scoring is exact match against gold answers — no LLM judge, so judging noise is eliminated by construction.

Pre-registered primary contrasts, reported uncorrected: (1) breadth hybrid vs pure top-k retrieval (HotpotQA), (2) breadth hybrid vs pure playbook, (3) breadth routing vs usage-frequency routing under skewed history, (4) the breadth coefficient in the E1 placement regression, (5) the same-direction replication of (1) and (3) on MuSiQue. Every other cellwise contrast is Holm-corrected within its experiment. Token matching is enforced on logged realized prompt tokens (means within 5%), and each headline number is additionally shown on an accuracy-versus-tokens curve with item-level bootstrap CIs, so no single matched point carries the argument.

Noise floor: the pure-retrieval cell is rerun in full (n=800) as a **null replicate** — relabelled as a treatment and compared against itself — and two key cells are re-scored under three fresh seeds at n=400. Nothing is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of that null distribution. The playbook merge is stochastic, so merged blocks are regenerated with three seeds for the hybrid and pure playbook; a difference must exceed twice the across-merge SD.

Power: n=800 paired at ~12% discordance gives ~80% power at ≈2.5 EM points (n=600 ⇒ ≈2.9), which is why P2–P4 are stated at ≥3 / ≥3.5. E1 uses n=150 per item (per-item MDE ~7 points), so no per-item claim is made; the hierarchical model borrows strength across 14 items and the slope is the tested quantity. E8's difference-of-differences is the least-powered primary test and is reported with its CI; if the CI spans zero we report the fixed-k-specificity question as open rather than resolved. Retrieval k, similarity cutoff and breadth cutoff are calibrated on the disjoint validation split; breadth is computed only on the unlabeled calibration split; held-out data is never used for tuning except in the two explicitly-labeled oracle arms, which are reported as ceilings and never as methods.
Preprint Collision Check:
**The literature search run for this proposal returned zero results.** The web search tool failed on every invocation with a server-side "tool use limit exceeded" error, including on a minimal test query, across multiple retries. No titles, dates, venues or abstracts were retrieved. I state plainly: **novelty has not been verified, only asserted.** Silence from a broken tool is not evidence of novelty, and this proposal should be read as having an open, unresolved collision risk. Two rounds of review have flagged this; I cannot fix it with prose and will not pretend otherwise.

**Closest work, from recollection only, explicitly unverified:** MemGPT (core/archival paging with usage- and recency-triggered promotion into an always-resident tier), A-MEM (consolidation under capacity pressure), Dynamic Cheatsheet (Suzgun et al., 2025) and agentic-context-engineering playbooks, ExpeL (AAAI 2024), Agent Workflow Memory (ICML 2025), ReasoningBank-style 2025/26 banks, MIPROv2 (EMNLP 2024) and GEPA. Beyond the LLM literature, the closest *conceptual* prior work — named by a reviewer and now conceded in Related Work — is classical cache admission and replacement: Belady's optimal algorithm, LFU/LRU/ARC, and working-set estimation, which already formalize "route residency by predicted future access, not stale historical frequency."

**Assessment of collision.** On the *decision problem* (where should an item live), MemGPT-style usage promotion collides directly, and we now run it as a first-class baseline (E2 v, E4) rather than a foil. On the *statistic* (deployment-distribution coverage rather than historical frequency), working-set estimation collides at the level of principle; we do not claim that principle as new. What we claim is not covered by either: (a) the tiers are not latency-equivalent — promotion changes prompt content and a miss costs an answer, not a delay; (b) the competitive tier is always exactly full, so admission is eviction on every query; (c) **the optimal move is inverted relative to caching** — a hit-rate-maximizing cache promotes broad items to serve them, whereas we predict the payoff is the vacated slot, which is precisely what the refill / no-refill / padding controls at k=2 test and what no caching or paging paper has reason to run; (d) coverage dominating *utility* is not a caching prediction at all, since caches optimize hit rate rather than downstream value.

**Unresolved risk.** A mid-2025-to-present preprint in the context-engineering / memory-tiering line proposing hot-cold promotion of frequently retrieved memory items into a static prompt, or token-budget-aware allocation between instruction and retrieval, is a natural next step in the ACE/ReasoningBank lineage and I cannot rule it out.

**Commitment.** Before any submission we will run and publish a dated search log — arXiv cs.CL/cs.AI, Semantic Scholar, and citation-forward from MemGPT, ACE/Dynamic Cheatsheet, ReasoningBank and MIPROv2 — over: "memory promotion always-on context agent"; "hot cold memory tiering LLM agent"; "instruction vs retrieval placement distilled experience"; "injection budget allocation agent memory"; "context budget routing playbook retrieval"; "coverage-based memory consolidation agent". If a collision is found, the surviving contribution is the part such a preprint is unlikely to have: the item-level placement regression with breadth, utility and usage entered as competing predictors; the refill/no-refill/padding controls identifying slot competition; the oracle-placement ceiling; and the threshold-retrieval difference-of-differences bounding the mechanism to fixed-k admission. **If a collision is found that also runs those controls, we withdraw the claim rather than reframe it.**
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Unverified novelty.** The search tool failed; the closest-work list is recollection. This is the largest single risk to the proposal and is stated in the Preprint Collision Check rather than softened.
2. **Gate risk.** The study is conditional on the bank mattering at all (E0). If top-k memory is indistinguishable from no memory in either direction, there is no placement question and we report the matched-token comparison as a bounded null with a stated MDE.
3. **Collapsed statistics.** If ρ(b,f) > 0.7 despite the deliberately skewed history stream, P4's frequency arm is uninformative and we say so rather than reinterpreting. Same rule for breadth vs utility. The pre-registered fallback (transparently augmenting the bank with synthetic high-utility narrow and low-utility broad items to decorrelate) is labeled secondary and would support a mechanism claim, not a deployment claim.
4. **Novelty risk against MemGPT and against caching theory.** If usage-frequency promotion matches breadth routing, the contribution reduces to a measured explanation of an existing heuristic plus the slot-competition mechanism. We keep the hypothesis and accept the reduced claim; we refuse to rescue it by broadening the paper into a generic memory survey.
5. **Threshold retrieval could dissolve the premise.** E8 tests this directly. If variable-cutoff retrieval matches the hybrid at matched tokens, the slot-scarcity framing is specific to fixed-k admission and that becomes the headline correction. Note that fixed-k is what deployed systems actually use, so this outcome is informative rather than vacuous — but it is a genuine refutation of the general framing.
6. **One task family.** HotpotQA plus MuSiQue is a dataset-level replication, not cross-family generality; web/tool and code agents are untested. We will not claim generality across task families, and this limitation appears in the abstract. Adding a second family did not fit the envelope; we chose a second dataset and a second retrieval architecture instead, on the grounds that the mechanism claim is about retrieval geometry rather than task semantics.
7. **One model.** Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct only; the 14B check was cut to fund the reviewer-named additions. Scaling behaviour of slot competition is unknown.
8. **Underpowered mechanism contrasts.** P3 needs a ≥4-point total effect at k=2 to separate refill from no-refill; P7's difference-of-differences is the least-powered primary test. If either is small we report the question as open, not settled.
9. **Attention dilution.** Long always-on playbooks may dilute attention independently of placement; the neutral-text length control bounds but does not eliminate this.
10. **Oracle arms touch held-out labels.** E6 is explicitly a ceiling, never a proposed method, and is excluded from all matched-token headline comparisons except as an upper bound.
